# Pose models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

26 pose models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image and a box per person. Output: keypoints with confidence scores for every person.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 1080x1920: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

<a id="rtmpose"></a>

## RTMPose

OpenMMLab's RTMPose (t, s, m, l; 256x192 and 384x288): real-time top-down 2D human pose, a CSPNeXt CNN with a SimCC head, trained on seven public pose datasets; also the whole-body DWPose and RTMW checkpoints (133 keypoints with feet, face and hands). Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

- Original code: <https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmpose> at `5408bc76f5b8`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`

- Training data: COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations), AI Challenger human keypoints (2017), CrowdPose, MPII Human Pose, sub-JHMDB (J-HMDB), Halpe-FullBody, PoseTrack 2018, ImageNet-1k (ILSVRC 2012 classification) (body7: COCO, AI Challenger, CrowdPose, MPII, sub-JHMDB, Halpe and PoseTrack18 keypoints; the CSPNeXt backbone was pre-trained on ImageNet-1k (and on the same pose data, `pt-body7`))
  - `dwpose-t`: COCO-WholeBody, UBody (upper-body whole-body keypoints, from OSX), COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations), AI Challenger human keypoints (2017), ImageNet-1k (ILSVRC 2012 classification) (COCO-WholeBody and UBody whole-body keypoints, distilled from a larger RTMPose (DWPose two-stage distillation); the CSPNeXt backbone was pre-trained on ImageNet-1k and on AI Challenger + COCO body keypoints)
  - `dwpose-s`: COCO-WholeBody, UBody (upper-body whole-body keypoints, from OSX), COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations), AI Challenger human keypoints (2017), ImageNet-1k (ILSVRC 2012 classification) (COCO-WholeBody and UBody whole-body keypoints, distilled from a larger RTMPose (DWPose two-stage distillation); the CSPNeXt backbone was pre-trained on ImageNet-1k and on AI Challenger + COCO body keypoints)

### Measured

Top-down on the ground-truth person boxes (non-crowd, at least one labelled keypoint), no flip test; people ranked by the mean of their 17 keypoint scores (not mmpose's rescoring and OKS-NMS), so not the papers' AP; pycocotools OKS AP; whole-body models scored on their 17 body keypoints. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
